name: Pulmonary Veno-Occlusive Disease and Pulmonary Capillary Haemangiomatosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, radiological, and histopathological findings

criteria.description: Histological evidence of widespread occlusion of small pulmonary veins and/or proliferation of pulmonary capillaries
High-resolution CT showing centrilobular ground-glass opacities, septal lines, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy
Pulmonary arterial hypertension confirmed by right heart catheterization with elevated pulmonary vascular resistance
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as left heart disease or chronic thromboembolic disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical clinical presentation with pulmonary hypertension, characteristic radiological findings, and histopathological confirmation or strong clinical suspicion with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Lung biopsy is gold standard but often high risk; diagnosis often presumptive based on imaging and clinical features

searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity
severe high blood pressure in lung arteries
very high pressure in lungs' blood vessels
low oxygen levels not improving with oxygen therapy
oxygen therapy failing to raise blood oxygen
fatigue due to poor oxygen levels

common.symptomName: Peripheral edema due to right heart failure
searchTerms: swelling in legs from heart problems
ankle puffiness due to heart failure

occasional.symptomName: Chest discomfort or pleuritic chest pain

searchTerms: sudden loss of consciousness at rest

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary edema precipitated by vasodilator therapy
searchTerms: lung fluid buildup triggered by blood vessel dilators
fluid in lungs caused by vasodilator drugs

laboratory: Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating right heart strain
imaging: High-resolution CT showing centrilobular ground-glass opacities, septal thickening, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy
Echocardiography demonstrating right ventricular hypertrophy and elevated pulmonary artery pressures
Right heart catheterization confirming pulmonary arterial hypertension with elevated pulmonary vascular resistance
genetic: Mutations in EIF2AK4 gene associated with familial cases
other: Lung biopsy showing occlusion of small pulmonary veins and capillary proliferation (gold standard but high risk)

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of venous occlusion or capillary proliferation on histology
Different radiological pattern without septal lines or lymphadenopathy
Better response to pulmonary vasodilator therapy
Presence of thromboembolic material on imaging

redFlags: Rapid progression of pulmonary hypertension despite therapy
Development of pulmonary edema after initiation of pulmonary vasodilators
Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen supplementation
references: Montani D, et al. Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease. Eur Respir J. 2009;33(1):189-200.
